(At Present Lodged In Dist. Jail, Banswara)
 ----Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Laxman S/o Rangji, R/o Dabdimal, P.s. Ambapura, Distt.
 Banswara Raj.
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Hemank Vaishnav For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, PP
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 12/11/2024 1.

This application for bail under Section 483 of BNSS has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.83/2024, registered at Police Station Ambapura, District Banswara, for offences under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) & 376(2)
(n) of IPC; Section 5(l)/6 of POCSO Act.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the statements of victim 'S' have already been recorded before the competent Criminal Court on 26.09.2024 as PW-1.
4.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the Court statements of the victim 'S', learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the victim 'S' in her Court's statements has not supported the Kailu @ Kailash vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:45616) on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175415889/
1 [2024:RJ-JD:45616] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-9600/2024] prosecution story and has turned hostile.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel further contended that in view of the fact that statements of victim 'S' have already been recorded before the competent criminal Court, there are no chances of the petitioner influencing her.

5. Lastly, learned counsel contended that the petitioner who is aged about 21 years is in judicial custody since 20.04.2024 and the statements of the victim 'S' have already been recorded; the trial against the petitioner is likely to consume sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused- petitioner.
6.
Per-Contra, learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the bail application.
However he was not in a position to refute the fact that the victim 'S' in her statements recorded as PW1 has not supported the prosecution story and has turned hostile.

7. Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that the petitioner who is aged about 21 years is in judicial custody so also the fact that the victims in her Court statements has not supported the prosecution story and has turned hostile.

This Court also prima facie finds that the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the remaining prosecution witnesses or fleeing away from justice, in case he is enlarged on bail, thus without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioners on bail.
[2024:RJ-JD:45616] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-9600/2024] Consequently, the second bail application under Section 483 of BNSS is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Kailu @ Kailash S/o Sh.
Dahleng arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.83/2024, registered at Police Station Ambapura,
District Banswara, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial Court, for his appearance before that Court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 37-mohit/-
